name: Fishing Rod
desc: A split-cane rod with a reel that clicks like a nervous knee. Face open water and press Confirm to cast.

name: Match Rod
desc: A proper telescopic carbon match rod. Finer tip, wider sweet spot on the bite bar, better odds of something worth the photograph.

name: Brown Trout
desc: Speckled, suspicious and fond of cold, clean rivers. Fly fishers talk about it the way other people talk about football.

name: Roach
desc: Silver, red-finned and the first fish of many a childhood. Rarely worth a fuss, always worth a photograph.

name: Perch
desc: Stripy, spiny on the back and a bit of a bruiser for its size. Lives in lakes and slow rivers.

name: Pike
desc: A long green ambush predator with a face like a disappointed solicitor. Handle with respect and long-nosed pliers.

name: Grayling
desc: The Lady of the Stream, named for her tall, sail-like dorsal fin. Prefers cool, fast, clean water.

name: Chub
desc: A fat-headed river fish that will eat almost anything and fight rather less than you hoped.

name: European Eel
desc: Born in the Sargasso Sea, spends years in our rivers, then goes all the way back. Puts your commute in perspective.

name: Atlantic Salmon
desc: Leaps weirs to get home to the river it was born in. Famously better at navigation than you are.

name: Arctic Charr
desc: A relic of the Ice Age, still living in a few deep, cold lakes in Scotland, Wales, Ireland and the Lakes.

name: Tench
desc: The doctor fish, folklore says, though no tench has ever held a surgery. Likes weedy, warm ponds.

name: Mackerel
desc: Striped, oily and in a hurry. Swims in shoals near the surface, mostly in summer, and is excellent grilled.

name: Cod
desc: The fish half the chip shops are named for. Heavy, white-fleshed and a bit sniffy about warm water.

name: Haddock
desc: Marked with a dark thumbprint above each pectoral fin, which legend ties to St Peter. A proper smoked-fish fish.

name: Pollack
desc: Hangs about rocky reefs and kelp, and fights hard for a fish with such a sulky lower jaw.

name: Plaice
desc: A flatfish with orange spots, lying camouflaged on sand and pretending to be a pavement.

name: European Sea Bass
desc: Silver, strong and fond of surf, estuaries and harbour walls. A prize for patient anglers.

name: Herring
desc: The silver darling. Once so plentiful that whole towns were built on it, and kippers still taste of them.

name: Whiting
desc: A slim, silver cousin of the cod. Cats approve.

name: Conger Eel
desc: A muscular sea eel that lives in wrecks and rocky holes. Looks like a drainpipe with opinions.

name: Thick-lipped Grey Mullet
desc: Cruises around harbours and estuaries with its mouth open, looking smug. Hard to hook and harder to impress.

name: Ballan Wrasse
desc: Colourful, tough and a resident of rocky shores. The males guard a seaweed nest.

name: Sea Trout
desc: A brown trout that went to sea for the buffet and came home bigger. Silver, and a connoisseur's catch.

name: Rudd
desc: Like a roach in a redder coat. Likes lakes and slow rivers, and showing off near the surface.

name: Gilthead Sea Bream
desc: A silver fish with a gold band between the eyes. A Mediterranean regular on Gibraltar's menus.

name: Sardine
desc: Small, silver and most at home in tins. Shoals in big numbers around the Mediterranean and the south-west.

name: Mahi-mahi
desc: A bright blue-green and gold fish that leaps, races and changes colour when caught. Also called dolphinfish, though no relation to dolphins.

name: Great Barracuda
desc: Long, silvery and toothy, with a fixed stare. Lurks near reefs and has a reputation it mostly deserves.

name: Bonefish
desc: A shallow-flat speedster that anglers chase for its first run alone. Called the ghost of the flats.

name: Yellowtail Snapper
desc: A pink-and-yellow reef fish with a bright yellow stripe and tail. Popular on Caribbean menus.

name: Blue Marlin
desc: A giant of open water with a spear for a nose. If you've hooked one from the shore, either you or the marlin has made a mistake.

name: Yellowfin Tuna
desc: A fast, powerful open-ocean tuna with yellow fins. Cruises warm tropical seas and is built for speed.

name: Wahoo
desc: One of the fastest fish in the sea, long and blue-barred, and gone before you've blinked.

name: Giant Trevally
desc: A big, bruising reef hunter of the Indian and Pacific oceans. Known to launch itself at seabirds.

name: Patagonian Toothfish
desc: Lives deep in cold southern waters and goes by Chilean sea bass on menus. Tightly managed around the Falklands and South Georgia.

name: Mackerel Icefish
desc: Its blood has almost no red cells, so it is oddly pale. Lives in the cold waters of the South Atlantic and Southern Ocean.

name: Antarctic Toothfish
desc: Makes its own antifreeze, which is handy off Antarctica. Grows large and slowly.
